react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: the eicosanoid synthesis / arachidonic acid metabolism axis. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' as the top hit (FDR = 2.12 × 10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment = 1250.9, 5 of 5 input eicosanoids detected in a 27-member pathway), with the same five metabolites replicating across nine SMPDB drug-action pathway mirrors at identical FDR. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00590 (Polyunsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis) as the top KEGG hit, again enriched for arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment independently awards 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) the strongest signal (p = 0.0067) with an 11/11 pathway hit-rate, and also returns 'Leukotriene metabolism' and 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' as significant sub-pathways (p = 0.043). Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol and xanthine do not cluster with the eicosanoid set and appear in distinct or non-significant pathway context — they are biological background in this dataset. The driver metabolites are five canonical arachidonic acid derivatives: the upstream substrate arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), the 5-lipoxygenase product leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), the 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) hydroxy-metabolites, and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717). Their coordinated differential abundance implicates 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) and cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) branch activity with downstream effector lipids including the PPARγ ligand 15d-PGJ2.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR = 2.12e-13, driven by five eicosanoids from the differential list: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. The fold-enrichment score of 1250.9 reflects the extreme concentration of eicosanoids relative to background. The same five metabolites appear in all ten SMPDB drug-action pathway mirrors returned by RaMP (Rofecoxib, Salicylate-sodium, Trisalicylate-choline, Acetaminophen, Acetylsalicylic Acid, Antipyrine, Antrafenine, Bromfenac, and Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency), all sharing FDR = 5.54e-13 and identical hit rosters, indicating that the signal is not pathway-specific but compounds-specific across NSAID-relevant biology. Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment awards Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) rank 1 with p = 8.40e-05 and an 11/11 hit-rate, confirming that the five input eicosanoids map to the empirical human-mfn network with complete pathway coverage. Leukotriene metabolism (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate) appear at ranks 3 and 4 with p = 0.015 and p = 0.024 respectively, corroborating the dual enzymatic branches. Arachidonic acid is the upstream substrate and the primary signal compound driving the cluster; the coordinated differential abundance of its derivatives implicates both the ALOX5 and COX branches of the eicosanoid cascade. Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol, and xanthine do not appear in any enriched pathway and are inferred to represent biological background noise distinct from the eicosanoid signal.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: the eicosanoid synthesis / arachidonic acid metabolism axis. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' as the top hit (FDR = 2.12 × 10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment = 1250.9, 5 of 5 input eicosanoids detected in a 27-member pathway), with the same five metabolites replicating across nine SMPDB drug-action pathway mirrors at identical FDR. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00590 (Polyunsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis) as the top KEGG hit, again enriched for arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment independently awards 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) the strongest signal (p = 0.0067) with an 11/11 pathway hit-rate, and also returns 'Leukotriene metabolism' and 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' as significant sub-pathways (p = 0.043). Thiosulfate, methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol and xanthine do not cluster with the eicosanoid set and appear in distinct or non-significant pathway context — they are biological background in this dataset. The driver metabolites are five canonical arachidonic acid derivatives: the upstream substrate arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), the 5-lipoxygenase product leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), the 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) hydroxy-metabolites, and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717). Their coordinated differential abundance implicates 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) and cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) branch activity with downstream effector lipids including the PPARγ ligand 15d-PGJ2.
